summary: 1939 90-foot Aermotor tower on the Dickenson/Russell County line, privately owned and listed standing; a 2003 auction record says removal was required, but 2008 and 2018 visits found it in place.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts says a January 2003 auction required removal; the 2008 and 2018 visit reports describe the tower as in place.

access.note: Administered by a private owner per the Register; the 2018 visit report says no sign is posted and the lower stairs were removed to prevent access to the cab.

visit.trail_note: Lower section of stairs removed to prevent access to the cab (2018 visit report); tower is beside a paved road.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts says a January 2003 auction sold the tower with removal required. Register visit reports from 2008 and 2018 describe the tower as in place, and the 2018 report is the most recent direct observation, so the record keeps standing.
The Register gives August 31, 1939 as the completion date; a 2008 visit report saw a concrete base dated 8/31/49. The story uses the Register's date and flags the base.

notes_for_editor: Brief's record had no height; NHLR gives a 90-foot tower, so height_m 27.4 is added. Staffing and condition come from two visitor reports on the Register (2008, 2018), not an official survey. The 2003 auction line rests on one Forest Lookouts sentence; two WebSearch rounds found no news or state record of the sale. Facebook and YouTube posts repeat the Register text and were not used. The Dickenson County photo gallery page (PID=83) rendered no text. Access: no sign, stairs removed to the cab per 2018; the story advises against climbing. No photos added: the Register credits photos to J.S. Harrison (2018) and to TheBigGiantHead through Krissy Reynolds, but no image URLs were read. Not verified: current owner's name, any removal order, whether the owner allows visits.
